Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Nexus Utilities Corp. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Nexus Utilities Corp.'s Q3 2024 Earnings Call. Joining me on the call today are Mark Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; John Ramirez, Chief Operating Officer; Emily Vargas, Chief Strategy Officer; Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer; and Tom Hargrove, Chief Regulatory Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that statements made during this call that are not historical facts are forward-looking statements and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied. Please refer to our SEC filings for a detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mark Thompson.

Mark Thompson: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on our performance this quarter. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities, delivering solid results in a challenging environment.

Our performance was driven by:
    1.  Key achievements and challenges during the quarter.
    2.  Retirement of fossil fuel plants and replacement strategies.
    3.  Progress on strategic initiatives and long-term goals.
    4.  Dividend policy and payout ratio strategy.
    5.  Earnings guidance for the next quarter and full year.
    6.  Rate base growth and factors impacting growth.
    7.  Updates on regulatory rate case filings and outcomes.

Let me provide some more detail on these seven key aspects.

Starting with our key achievements and challenges this quarter. Our diversified fleet of 25 GW across thermal, renewables, and storage delivered standout results, with adjusted EBITDA up 12% year-over-year to $850 million and adjusted EPS of $1.42, beating our guidance midpoint by 8%. Operationally, we hit record generation of 28.5 TWh, up 7%, thanks to 93.2% fleet availability—our best in five years. CCGTs in ERCOT and PJM ran at 68% capacity factor, dispatching 15% above plan in Texas heatwaves for $250 million in LMP uplift at $85/MWh averages, aided by $45 million in turbine refurbishments cutting outages to 1.5%. Renewables hit 32% of output, energizing 450 MW solar like the 250 MW Desert Sun in Arizona with a data center PPA, pushing our pipeline to 8 GW. Hybrids excelled, with a 200 MW solar-BESS in California at 92% capture and 89% efficiency via AI EMS, generating $30 million in CAISO ancillaries. Regulated revenues grew 10% to $1.2 billion from rate base expansion, capex hit $650 million for grid hardening earning $75 million FERC incentives, liquidity stands at $4.2 billion with 3.1x debt/EBITDA, and we returned $250 million via dividends and repurchases. We launched a 50 MW green hydrogen pilot with DOE funding for 20% blending by 2026, and data center PPAs now 25% of backlog. Challenges included gas spikes to $3.50/MMBtu trimming spark spreads, hedged at 70% to limit impact to $50 million; MISO basis losses of $15 million; CPUC NEM delays shifting $80 million revenue; FERC queues idling 1 GW; weather swings; supply chain inflating wind capex 8%; labor up 6%; and cyber threats met with $25 million zero-trust spend. These affirm our diversification, IRA credits of $150 million, and prep for 2025 EPS of $5.80-$6.20 with renewables at 40% EBITDA by 2030.

Next, our retirement of fossil fuel plants and replacement strategies. Our 8.8 GW fossil fleet—35% of capacity, averaging 45 years for coal and 20 for gas—is retiring strategically: 4.2 GW coal by 2027 starting with 1,200 MW Riverbend in Ohio, then 800 MW Blackhawk in Illinois, saving $250 million O&M annually with 8-10% EBITDA accretion net of $1.2 billion reserves. Gas peakers: 2.1 GW by 2028 including 600 MW ERCOT. Backed by IRP approvals, our $12 billion capex—60% green bonds/IRA—builds: 55% or $6.6 billion for 5.5 GW solar/wind like 1.2 GW Apex Solar Plains (ERCOT, 28% CF, 400 MW Tesla BESS at 85% firming), 800 MW PJM Vestas wind; 25% or $3 billion for 3 GW/12 GWh BESS like 500 MW LFP in MISO-South stacking revenues, 100 MW Form Energy iron-air; 15% or $1.8 billion for 1.5 GW H2-ready GE 7HA CCGTs and 900 MW CCUS at Gateway ($150 million 45Q); 5% or $600 million NuScale SMRs and H2 electrolyzers. Tailored regionally against duck curves, queues; economics at $25-35/MWh LCOE vs coal $50+, 10.5-11% ROE, 14% storage IRR, PPAs with Google/Microsoft. By 2030, fossils <10%, 70% emissions cut to 150 gCO2/kWh, 6-8% EPS growth.

On progress toward strategic initiatives and long-term goals under our three pillars—clean transition, grid resilience, sustainable growth—for net-zero by 2045 ahead of peers and 6-8% EPS CAGR via $15-18 billion capex. H1 added 450 MW renewables (300 MW Southeast solar, 150 MW PJM wind) to 8.2 GW or 42% of 19.5 GW fleet at 28% solar CF. BESS at 250 MW including 100 MW/400 MWh ERCOT for $45 million ancillaries, on track for 2 GW by 2027 at $35/MWh LCOE; 1.2 GW new PPAs with hyperscalers. Idled 400 MW MISO coal, cut intensity 15% to 350 lbs/MWh, repowered with 64% efficient H2-blendable turbines for 60% zero-emission by 2030. $1.2 billion T&D including AMI for 1.5 million customers, synchrophasors; FERC 2222 for $120 million DER; ERCOT peaker dispatch at $5,000/MWh, PJM capacity at $125/kW-year. 93% availability via analytics, 1.8% customer growth, 5,000 EV chargers, 200 MW data centers. Renewables EBITDA up 25% to $450 million at 12% ROIC, 18% FFO/debt. On track for 12 GW renewables/BESS, coal exit, 50% carbon-free; mitigations for supply/interconnection.

Lisa will cover the financial elements including dividend policy, earnings guidance, and rate base growth, while Tom will address regulatory updates.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Lisa Chen to discuss the financials.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, Mark. Good morning, everyone. For the Q3 2024, we reported earnings per share of $1.42 and revenue of $2.68 billion. Our financial performance reflects the strength of our diversified business model and our disciplined approach to capital allocation.

Our capital expenditure for the quarter was $650 million, primarily focused on renewables expansion and grid resilience. We remain committed to maintaining a strong balance sheet and returning value to shareholders. We anticipate 6-8% EPS growth through the decade.

Expanding on our dividend policy and payout ratio strategy, a cornerstone of our framework as a leader with over 15 GW across thermal, nuclear, renewables, and storage in Southeast, PJM, ERCOT. Target 60-70% of adjusted earnings, steady eight years, balancing returns and reinvestments. 2023 full-year $2.48/share, 28th consecutive increase at 4.5%, 5.1% decade CAGR like Southern/Duke. Q2 paid $0.62 quarterly, TTM 64.2% on $3.86 EPS, YTD 65.1% with $1.8 billion cash ops post $950 million capex. Calibrated for 90% predictable cash from 9.8% ROE, $50-60 billion sector capex; our $4.2 billion to 2028 for 1.2 GW solar-storage Georgia, Brunswick nuclear uprates, $500 million BESS for 3.5 GW renewables. Yield 4.1% vs index 3.4%. Sustainability test: FFO/debt >18%, coverage >1.7x (at 2.1x); $300 million repurchases YTD for 1-2% EPS; DRIP $45 million. Regional: Southeast 10.5% ROE for EV; PJM $120/MW-day; ERCOT 62% CCGT. Reaffirm 4-6% CAGR to $2.90+ by 2027 on 5-7% EPS, 60-70% payout.

On earnings guidance, Q4 2024 adjusted EPS $0.92-$0.98, 8% growth midpoint vs $0.87; revenues $2.65-$2.75 billion up 5%; EBITDA $1.05-$1.12 billion up 7%. Milder weather, 4% retail sales on 12% C&I/data centers; merchant $45-50/MWh PJM/MISO, nuclear 93% CF; gas hedges $2.75-3.00/MMBtu 85%; renewables 35% wind CF. O&M mitigated, capex $850 million. FY2025 EPS $4.05-$4.25 up 12%, revenues $11.2-$11.6 billion up 6%; regulated $7.8 billion/$3.2 billion EBITDA on $28 billion rate base +3.5%; competitive $2.9 billion/$1.1 billion; renewables/storage $800 million up 25% IRA PPAs. Northeast ISO-NE $12.50/kW-month $450 million; Texas 15% growth; Midwest upside. Pillars: $1.5 billion renewables M&A, $400 million grid tech VPPs, 60-70% FCF payout $0.75 quarterly 4.2% yield, $500 million buybacks. Assumes stable fuel/weather/reg; 2.5x debt/EBITDA.

Regarding rate base growth, at Q3 end $26.4 billion, up 6.2% YoY from $24.9 billion on $1.8 billion net adds, $1.2 billion TTM post $650 million dep. In-service up 5.4%, $120 million AFUDC at 5.2% rates. 2024 capex $2.1 billion/Q3 toward $2.4 billion: 35% transmission $630 million like PJM Greenline $450 million +$320 million +$25 million incentives, $800 million HVDC offshore; 45% distribution $810 million AMI 15,000 Ohio $250 million 10.5% ROE, $180 million 300 MW community BESS ITC; 20% generation $360 million 400 MW ERCOT solar PTC, 150 MW LFP. Northeast 7.1%, Midwest 5.8%, Texas indirect. $500 million coal securitization, 7.9% AFUDC, 95% domestic. Challenges: reg lag 9-12 months, 3.2% inflation. 2025-2029 $13.5 billion for 6-7% growth to $36 billion, DOE H2, 2 GW data centers.

John Ramirez: Thank you, Lisa. Let me provide an update on the operational front. We are seeing improved efficiency in our combined-cycle gas power plants due to the implementation of advanced predictive analytics. This has resulted in a 15% increase in output. Our outage rates are also down 22%.

Emily Vargas: Thank you, John. Turning to our long-term strategy, we are actively exploring opportunities in the battery storage and hydrogen space. We believe this will be a key driver of future growth. We are also evaluating potential acquisitions in the ERCOT and PJM markets.

Dr. Raj Patel: Thank you, Emily. From a technology perspective, we are making significant investments in grid modernization and cybersecurity. We recently deployed zero-trust architecture solutions to enhance our defenses against cyber threats. We are also piloting AI-driven energy management systems in our ERCOT operations.

Tom Hargrove: Thank you, Dr. Patel. On the regulatory front, we received approval for our Buckeye Solar-plus-Storage rate rider in Ohio. This will allow us to recover $212 million annually while advancing clean energy integration.

Mark Thompson: Thank you, Lisa, John, Emily, Raj, and Tom. Now, we'll open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Mike Larson with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Mike Larson: Good morning. Can you elaborate on your plans for data center load growth and its impact on your renewables pipeline?

Mark Thompson: Certainly, Mike. Data centers are a major tailwind, representing 25% of our PPA backlog now versus 10% last year, mirroring commitments like Microsoft's 10 GW push. We've signed MOUs for 200 MW in Virginia and more in Texas/Ohio, justifying capex with 24/7 carbon-free matching our nuclear and hybrids. Our 8 GW renewables pipeline, with 2.5 GW advanced, positions us to meet 3% CAGR load growth from AI/EVs.

Operator: Our next question comes from Priya Singh with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Priya Singh: What is your outlook for capex and its funding in 2025?

Lisa Chen: Thanks, Priya. We're guiding $2.8 billion for 2025 within our $13.5 billion 2025-2029 plan, focused on T&D, renewables, storage. Funding via 75/25 debt/equity, green bonds, IRA credits, securitizations—no dilution needed with 53% equity, A- ratings, $4.2 billion liquidity. ROIC targets 12%+.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Kim with RBC Capital. Please go ahead.

David Kim: How are you mitigating risks related to supply chain delays in turbine and battery procurement?

John Ramirez: Good question, David. We've locked 70% fixed-price EPC, 95% domestic sourcing for IRA bonuses, strategic partnerships like Siemens Gamesa/GE Vernova/CATL/Tesla. Apprenticeships address labor, $200 million SPP upgrades counter basis. Queue fast-tracks preserve 80% at-risk MW.

Operator: Our next question comes from Sarah Jenkins with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins: Thanks, and good morning everyone. Could you provide an update on your regulatory rate case filings and outcomes? Specifically, how these are tracking against your capex recovery needs for the clean energy transition?

Lisa Chen: Good morning, Sarah. Regulatory matters are central to our strategy serving 4.5 million customers in MISO-South, PJM, SPP. Recent: Ohio PUCO Q2 favorable—requested $285 million on $4.2 billion base for Buckeye 450 MW solar+200 MWh storage AFUDC, got $212 million (74%), 10.25% ROE up 50 bps, 75% CWIP grid hardening HTLS post-Uri. Flows 12 cents EPS, recovers Perry nuclear. Indiana IURC: $420 million ask $5.8 billion base EV chargers, got $345 million (82%), 10.35% ROE, formula rates renewables queue $800 million. Active: Kentucky PSC $310 million hearings, 75% interim $155 million Trimble 150 MWh flow BESS; Missouri PSC $520 million largest ever Resilient Grid 2035 undergrounding/AMI/100 MW Form Energy; Illinois Q1 2025 multi-year $650 million PBR SAIDI-linked. Midwest 70% CWIP approval up from 55%, Southeast pro-dispatchable; FERC 881 T&D. Supports 6-8% EPS, 92% capex recovery.

Mark Thompson: Thanks, Sarah. These underscore partnering for innovation like VPPs 50 MW Google Nest PJM DR. Amid 3% load, bills up 4.2% below average. Ahead with FERC-NEPSI hydro/CCUS 90% cuts by 2040.

Sarah Jenkins: Great detail—thanks. That's all for me.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the call back over to Mark Thompson for closing remarks.

Mark Thompson: Thank you. In summary, we delivered solid results in the Q3 2024, demonstrating the strength of our business model and our commitment to creating long-term value for our shareholders. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and positioning Nexus Utilities Corp. for continued success. Thank you for your time and interest in Nexus Utilities Corp.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
